(e) Underground cable for electric service. In subdivisions utilizing underground cable for electrical service, developers shall be required to accomplish the same items listed in subsection (d).
(f) Costs and assessments. The cost of providing and maintaining street light service after installation will be chargeable to Macon-Bibb County as set forth in chapter 29.

2412:
This Division of the Regulations for Subdivisions is hereby declared to be remedial and is intended to provide consistent requirements for the provision of sidewalks and associated improvements in Macon-Bibb County and further it is the purpose of this Division to secure the following objectives:
(1) To provide safe, convenient, and unobstructed paths for pedestrians.
(2) To provide for the necessary separation between pedestrians, vehicles, utilities and street furniture.
(3) To provide for safe and efficient driveways and street drainage.
(4) A clear delineation and protection of the public right-of-way.
(5) The recognition that walking as a physical fitness activity is becoming more popular.
(6) To establish and maintain pedestrian linkages within neighborhoods and between neighborhoods and: (a) other neighborhoods; (b) neighborhood commercial uses; (c) schools; and (d) community facilities such as libraries, churches, post offices, government offices, and other similar facilities.
(7) To provide alternative transportation options to reduce motor vehicle traffic thereby relieving traffic congestion, improving air quality, and other benefits.
(8) To establish and/or maintain an active street life the benefits of which may include crime reduction, critical social interaction, sense of community, and others.
These regulations shall apply to all new development approved after the adoption of these Regulations except that infill parcels in already approved subdivisions with no existing sidewalk shall not be subject to said provisions.
(Ord. No. O-19-0003, § 1(Exh. A), 2-5-2019)

The exceptions include receiving a variance from these standards which are allowed through the procedures established by these regulations. Previously constructed facilities shall be considered non-conforming and as such may be repaired and maintained but if and when replacement becomes necessary shall be replaced according to the standards or variance procedures of this Division. 2414:

Apartment complexes or other similar residential developments with private internal drives shall also provide sidewalks or pedestrian paths which meet all local, state and federal requirements for handicap access. Such internal walkways shall meet all local, state and federal requirements for handicap access. Where a walkway crosses an internal drive, a well-defined crosswalk shall be provided.

Other Areas characterized by mixed uses or any other configuration not provided in subsections (1) through (3) above, shall comply with either the regulations provided specifically for that development type, by a use by use application, or if neither of these methods is pertinent, by the analysis and recommendation of the Macon-Bibb County Engineer.

2416:
[Design and construction requirements as follows:]
(1) Permit Required. It is unlawful for any person to lay, construct, or build any sidewalk, driveway apron, or curb and gutter within Macon-Bibb County without securing a construction permit from the Macon-Bibb County Engineering Department. Such permits are in addition to grading or excavation permits required by Macon-Bibb County.
(2) Design Required. Upon application for a construction permit, the applicant shall submit a plan or sketch of the proposed construction which must be approved by the Macon-Bibb County Engineer prior to the issuance of a construction permit for sidewalk, driveway apron, or curb and gutter.
(3) Timing of Sidewalk Installation. Sidewalks shall be installed up front by the developer before any building permits are issued. The individual lot builder shall be required to remove a section of the sidewalk to install the driveway entrance once they have determined where the driveway will be placed.
(4) Duty to Repair and Replace. Upon detection of any defective sidewalk within one (1) year from the date of construction, The Macon-Bibb County Engineer shall cause a notice to be served upon the bonded contractor or bonded property owner directing that repairs and/or replacement shall be accomplished within a designated period of time. Failure to comply with the terms of this notice shall cause forfeiture of bond. If it is determined that other parties are responsible for damage to the sidewalk, such as an individual home builder, the Department of Business Development shall cause the repair to be made by the appropriate contractor and withhold the certificate of occupancy until the repair is made.
(5) Use Standards.
a. All sidewalk design plans submitted must show provision for the mobility, safety, and comfort of the pedestrian.
b. All sidewalk design plans submitted must show provision for adequate pedestrian access to abutting properties and shall show how the connection to the abutting sidewalk will be accomplished.
c. All new sidewalks shall meet or exceed standards for handicapped access set by the Americans with Disabilities Act and any other applicable federal, state or local standards.
(6) Design and Construction Standards and Procedures.
a. Design and Construction Standards. The design and construction of all new sidewalks shall comply with the latest standard specifications of the Georgia Department of Transportation, and reference shall be made to the latest edition of "A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets," and "The Guide for Planning, Design and Operation of Pedestrian Facilities," both published by the American Association of State Highway and Transportation Officials (AASHTO).
b. Landscape Strip. A minimum two-foot landscape strip shall be provided between the back of the curb and gutter and front of the sidewalk. In areas of heavy pedestrian use this landscape strip may be constructed of concrete, decorative pavers, or any other material approved by the Macon-Bibb County Engineer. In no case shall a sidewalk be constructed against the back of the curb without a landscape strip unless first approved by the Macon-Bibb County Engineer. If no curb and gutter is installed, a two-foot landscape strip shall be provided between the edge of the street/road and the sidewalk.
c. Sidewalk Location. On all streets, a minimum five (5) [foot] wide sidewalk shall be provided on both sides of the road to promote a balanced and multimodal transportation system that serves the mobility needs of all segments of the population and complies with latest edition of The Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (ADA).
d. Site Preparation and Inspection. The Macon-Bibb County Engineer shall be given one (1) working day's notice before any material is placed in order that an inspection may be made of the sub-grade, the forms, and the spacing for expansion-contraction joints. The excavating and grading shall be smoothly and neatly done, and to the proper depth, all large stones, boulders, roots, other vegetation, and rubbish of every description being removed from the sub-grade and the entire work made to conform to the profile and grade of the walk when finished. Soft, spongy, or loamy areas in the sub-grade must be removed, and the space refilled with stable material thoroughly compacted
(Ord. No. O-19-0003, § 1(Exh. A), 2-5-2019)
2417:
(a) Formal Variances. Upon application by the owner or agent of the property, the Macon-Bibb County Engineer may choose to grant a variance from any requirements of this chapter if it is found that:
(1) The area has been recognized as having historical, archaeological, and/or architectural significance by Macon-Bibb County, the State of Georgia, or the United States of America and in order to maintain such significance, a variance is appropriate.
(2) There are pre-existing obstructions that cannot be easily relocated and should not be altered, such as water courses and/or natural topographic features and no reasonable alternative is available to accommodate the sidewalk.
(b) Administrative Variances.
(1) Where sufficient right-of-way is not available, the Macon-Bibb County Engineer may set a special sidewalk location standard within the right-of-way or if sufficient right-of-way is not available or is only large enough to accommodate utilities in their most efficient placement, sidewalk easements may be established, provided that sufficient front yard setback area exists. Sidewalk easements must be granted in perpetuity for public access. Such easements shall be wide enough to accommodate the required sidewalk width plus one additional foot on each side of the facility. Such easements shall be clearly indicated on all plats and protected via the use of covenants clearly stated on the plat and each relevant property deed stating the right to unimpeded public access in perpetuity. Sidewalks in easements shall match with sidewalks in adjacent developments and right-of-way cross sections must show match lines. The Macon-Bibb County Engineer must definitively determine that within the established right-of-way, that sidewalks cannot be accommodated even if the road were narrowed from curb to curb to the minimum required.
(2) The normal dimensional requirements and location of the sidewalk may be adjusted at the approval of the Macon-Bibb County Engineer to accommodate or preserve a specimen tree, provided however, that public access easements are granted if the location of the sidewalk is moved off the public right-of-way.
(3) The normal dimensional requirements and location of the sidewalk may be adjusted at the approval of the Macon-Bibb County Engineer to accommodate, preserve, or avoid undue impacts to signage, utilities or landscaping in an area where signage, utilities or mature landscaping is existing and part of the established neighborhood character, provided however, that public access easements are granted if the location of the sidewalk is moved off the public right-of-way.

(b) For the taxable year 1981, and each subsequent taxable year, Macon-Bibb County does hereby grant to each person who is 65 years of age or over an exemption from ad valorem taxes, if any, levied by Macon-Bibb County that relate solely to a special tax district defined by the corporate limits of the former City of Macon, Georgia as it existed just prior to the creation of the restructured government in an amount of $2,000.00 on a homestead owned and occupied by him or her as a residence if his or her net income, together with the net income of his or her spouse who also occupies and resides at the homestead, as net income is defined by the state constitution, from all sources, except as provided in this subsection, does not exceed $8,000.00 for the immediately preceding taxable year for income tax purposes. For the purpose of this subsection, net income shall not include income received as retirement, survivor or disability benefits under the federal social security act or under any other public or private retirement, disability or pension system, except such income which is in excess of the maximum amount authorized to be paid to an individual and his spouse under the federal social security act, and income from such sources in excess of the maximum amount shall be included as net income for the purposes of this subsection. The value of the residence in excess of the above-exempted amount shall remain subject to taxation. No taxpayer shall receive the benefits of the homestead exemption unless he or she, or his or her agent, files or has filed, an affidavit with the tax commissioner, giving his or her age and the amount of income which he or she and his or her spouse received during the last taxable year for income tax purposes, and such additional information relative to receiving the benefits of such exemption as will enable the tax commissioner to determine whether the taxpayer is entitled to an exemption. The tax commissioner shall provide affidavit forms for this purpose. The applications shall be processed in the same manner as other applications for homestead exemptions, and the provisions of law, including the provisions of this article applicable to the processing of homestead exemptions, as the same now exist or may hereafter be amended, shall apply thereto. It shall be the duty of any taxpayer, however, to notify the tax commissioner in the event he becomes ineligible for any reason for the exemption provided in this subsection.
2435:
(a) Any taxpayer who returned or paid taxes in Macon-Bibb County for the preceding tax year and who fails to return his property for taxation as provided in section 26-25 shall be deemed to have returned for taxation, for the current tax year, the same property as was returned or was deemed to have been returned, in the preceding tax year at the same valuation as the property was finally determined for the preceding year.
(b) Any penalty prescribed in this section for the failure of a taxpayer to return his property for taxation within the time provided by law shall apply only to the property which the taxpayer did not return prior to the expiration of making returns and which he has acquired since his last return or which represents improvements on previously existing property since his last return or any return which he is deemed to have made.
(c) Nothing contained in this article shall be deemed to preclude the board from raising or lowering the valuation of property for tax purposes in any proper case.
(d) Notwithstanding the provisions of subsection (a), taxpayers owning tangible personal property subject to taxation are nevertheless required to file an annual statement of such assets. It shall be reported upon a statement of business assets form as the same may from time to time be prescribed, and shall be filed on or prior to April 1 of each year as prescribed by sections 26-22 and 26-25.
2436:
(a) There is hereby created a board of tax assessors for Macon-Bibb County (the "board"), which shall consist of five persons appointed by Macon-Bibb County who shall serve for terms of six years each, provided that members of the joint board of tax assessors for Bibb County who are on that joint board as of December 31, 2013 shall serve out their original terms as members of that joint board on the board of tax assessors for Macon-Bibb County prior to being subject to reappointment. Assessors may succeed themselves if reappointed and may be removed by Macon-Bibb County during a term only for cause shown for the failure to perform duties or requirements or meet the qualifications imposed upon such member by law including, but not limited to, the duties, requirements, and qualifications specified pursuant to O.C.G.A. §§ 48-5-295, 48-5-295.1, 48-5-262(e) and 48-5-296.
(b) All staff and employees of the Macon-Bibb County board of tax assessors shall be positions of employment covered by the personnel policies and procedures applicable to employees of Macon-Bibb County; provided, however, that in applying the Macon-Bibb County personnel policies and procedures, any chief appraiser designated by the board of assessors pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 48-5-264(a) shall be treated as a department head and shall not be covered by the Macon-Bibb County problem solving procedure.

2437:
(a) If any taxpayer shall acquire any taxable property which was not included in the taxpayer's return for the preceding calendar year and which is held by such taxpayer on January 1 of the current calendar year, it shall be the duty of the taxpayer to make a return thereof as provided in section 26-27.
(b) If a taxpayer shall make improvements to any taxable property which improvements were made since the taxpayer's return or deemed return of the property for the preceding calendar year, with respect to property held by such taxpayer of the current calendar year, it shall nevertheless be the duty of the taxpayer to make a new return and to reflect thereon the value of the improvements made or added to the property since January 1 of the preceding calendar year.
(c) Upon a failure of the taxpayer to make a return of newly acquired property or of newly improved property, it shall be the duty of the board to assess it in the name of the current owner thereof according to the best information available to the board. The property owner shall be given notice of such assessment and shall have the right of review thereof as provided in sections 26-25 and 26-28.
2438: All returns of property, real or personal, for ad valorem taxes for Macon-Bibb County or state tax purposes shall be transmitted by the tax commissioner to the board for review, and the board shall review each such return for accuracy and completeness, and for the correctness of valuations of the property returned thereon.
2439: The lien of taxes collectible under the provisions hereof shall date from January 1 of the year in which the taxes become due, and the lien of such taxes shall be a special lien on the property upon which the same are due and a general lien against all property of the taxpayer owning the same.
2440:
(a) Should the board find that a taxpayer has failed to return real or personal property for taxation when he or she is legally liable to do so or that he or she has substantially undervalued property which he or she has returned for taxation or that property which he or she is deemed to have returned for taxation is substantially undervalued, the board shall cause the return to be amended or the property assessed at its correct value.
(b) If a taxpayer has filed a return or is deemed to have filed a return which does not provide an appropriate valuation considering improvements made to the property, the board shall likewise cause the return to be amended so as to reflect the improvements or shall cause the property to be assessed accordingly.
(c) Whenever, under the provisions of this article, the board amends a return or assesses property, the taxpayer shall be given written notice of the amendment or assessment. If the taxpayer filed a return or was deemed to have filed a return, such notice shall be given as provided in section 26-34.
2441:
(a) Whenever the board shall determine that property subject to taxation is not returned or deemed to have been returned for taxation and is consequently not valued or assessed for tax purposes, or if it is substantially undervalued (if returned or deemed to have been returned) by reason of improvements not previously taken into consideration, it shall be the duty of the board to assess the same at its fair market value.
(b) In making such an assessment, the board shall not only assess the property for the then-current calendar year, but shall assess the same for all prior years, up to seven, that the property was not returned for taxation or was not deemed returned for taxation.
(c) If, during any review, the board determines that improvements have been made to property subject to taxation within the last seven years which increased the value of the property, which increased value rendered the property substantially undervalued in any return within a seven-year period or rendered it undervalued for any year during which the improvements existed on January 1 of that year for property deemed to have been returned, the board shall make a like assessment to reflect the increase in value. Payment of a tax bill for any given year shall not be deemed to preclude the subsequent assessment nor increase in an assessment of property by the board, provided that no such assessment or increase in assessment shall extend further back than seven years.
(d) In addition to the taxes determined to be due thereon, the tax commissioner shall add to that amount a penalty of ten percent or the sum of $1.00, whichever is greater.
2442: Whenever the board has assessed property at a valuation different from that at which it was returned or was deemed to have been returned, or when the board assesses unreturned property, it shall give notice to the taxpayer as provided in O.C.G.A. § 48-5-306.
2443: Any taxpayer may appeal from an assessment or change in valuations as returned made by the board and have a tax assessment pertaining to his property reviewed by a board of equalization. Proceedings for the establishment of the board of equalization and review of assessments shall proceed as provided in O.C.G.A. § 48-5-311.
2444: As soon as practicable after January 2 in each year, the board shall commence to review the valuations reflected by tax returns, the value of all property deemed to have been returned and the value of property not returned or deemed to have been returned. As promptly thereafter as practicable, the board shall transmit the returns and assessments, as finally approved by them after notice to the taxpayer, to the tax commissioner to enable him to prepare a digest.
2445: The tax commissioner shall forthwith proceed to complete the preparation of a tax digest which may be in such form as he from time to time may prescribe but which will also conform to the requirements of the state revenue commissioner for tax digests generally. The tax commissioner shall, as soon as possible, advise the commission of the amount of the digest.
2446: As soon thereafter as possible, the commission and the Bibb County board of education shall determine their respective millage rates, and such rates all be forthwith communicated to the tax commissioner to enable him to submit the digest to the state revenue commissioner.
2447: Upon completion of the tax digest and fixing of millage rates by the commission and Macon-Bibb County board of education, the same shall be transmitted to the state revenue commissioner for his approval, and, when the same shall have been approved, the tax commissioner shall promptly prepare and mail tax bills.
2448:
(a) Taxes payable under the provisions hereof shall be due and payable upon receipt of the bill; provided, however, that one-half of the taxes shall be due and payable in any event 30 days following the mailing of the bills, and the remaining one-half shall be due and payable on November 15 in each year with interest at the rate of one percent per month or portion thereof, or $1.00, whichever is greater, after 60 days from the date of mailing of tax bills with respect to the first installment, and after November 15 in each year with respect to the second installment; provided, that no interest shall be due on either installment until 60 days shall have elapsed from the mailing of the tax bills.

2449: A penalty of ten percent of the tax due shall accrue on taxes not paid on or before December 20 of each year, and interest shall accrue at the rate specified in O.C.G.A. § 48-2-40 on the total amount of unpaid taxes and penalty until both the taxes and penalty are paid. The tax commissioner shall issue executions for such taxes, penalty, and interest against each delinquent taxpayer in their respective counties. The ten percent penalty shall be paid over to the county fiscal authority to assist the county in paying the expense of collecting the delinquent taxes.

2451: The tax commissioner is hereby authorized and empowered to prescribe administrative procedures not in conflict herewith which are reasonably required to administer the return, assessment and collection of taxes hereunder.

Taxes collected and required to be remitted to the Macon-Bibb County board of education shall be paid over in like fashion.
2453: The compensation for the tax commissioner, the board and the employees of the tax commissioner and the board shall be fixed by the commission.
2454: While this article attempts to specify in some detail the method of returning and assessing property for taxation in Macon-Bibb County, the review of assessments and the method for billing and collecting taxes which are due, it is recognized that it may not be complete in every respect, and if matters arise not covered by or comprehended in this article, the provisions of the state public revenue code shall apply.
2455: The tax commissioner is authorized and requested to retain for the use of Macon-Bibb County ten percent of all taxes collected in excess of 80 percent of the total taxes due according to the net tax digest for the year 1951 and until further order of the board and these commissions, and such taxes shall be covered into the county treasury.
2456:
(a) Pursuant to the authority vested in the commission, there is hereby exempted from ad valorem taxation, including all such taxes levied for educational purposes and for state purposes, the following types of tangible personal property:
(1) Inventory of goods in the process of manufacture or production, which shall include all partly finished goods and raw materials held for direct use or consumption in the ordinary course of a taxpayer's manufacturing or production business in the state. This exemption shall apply only to tangible personal property which is substantially modified, altered or changed in the ordinary course of the taxpayer's manufacturing, processing or production operations in this state.
(2) Inventory of finished goods manufactured or produced within the state in the ordinary course of a taxpayer's manufacturing or production business when held by the original manufacturer or producer of such finished goods. The exemption provided for such finished goods shall be for a period not exceeding 12 months from the date such property is produced or manufactured.
(3) Inventory of finished goods which, on January 1, are stored in a warehouse, dock or wharf, whether public or private, and which are destined for shipment to a final destination outside the state, and inventory of finished goods which are shipped into the state from outside this state and stored for transshipment to a final destination outside this state. The exemption provided for in this section shall be for a period not exceeding 12 months from the date such property is stored in this state. All property that is claimed to be exempt under the provisions of this subsection shall be designated as being "in transit" upon the official books and records of the warehouse, dock or wharf, whether public or private, where such property is being stored. Such official books and records shall contain a full, true, and accurate inventory of all such property, including the date of the receipt of the property, the date of the withdrawal of the property, the point of origin of the property, and the point of final destination of the same, if known. The official books and records of any such warehouse, dock or wharf, whether public or private, pertaining to any such "in transit" property, shall at all times be open to the inspection of all taxing authorities of this state and of any political subdivision of this state.
(b) As used in this section, the following words shall have the meanings ascribed to them:
(1) Finished goods means goods, wares and merchandise of every character and kind, but shall not include unrecovered, unextracted or unsevered natural resources, or raw materials, or goods in the process of manufacture or production, or the stock-in-trade of a retailer.
(2) Raw materials means any material, whether crude or processed, that can be converted by manufacture, processing or combination into a new and useful product, but shall not include unrecovered, unextracted or unsevered natural resources.
(c) Nothing contained in this section shall be deemed to undertake to modify the provisions of a constitutional amendment respecting exemption from ad valorem taxation of certain agricultural products described in 1974 Ga. Laws, page 1706.
(d) The extent of exemption from taxation of tangible personal property described in this section shall be 100 percent thereof.
(e) The exemption from taxation provided in this section shall apply to ad valorem taxes for the calendar year 1984 and all subsequent years until changed by proper action of the commission.
2457:
(a) All real property which is purchased at tax sales in the name of the Macon-Bibb County is declared to be surplus immediately upon its acquisition, whether the property has heretofore or may hereafter be so acquired.
(b) Subject to the provisions of state law respecting redemption of property acquired at tax sales, whenever a request is made to Macon-Bibb County to sell property, the request shall be referred to the Macon-Bibb County attorney who shall determine the minimum bid value thereof, which may be less then fair value, as determined by the current or previous tax value as set by the tax assessors, whichever is higher, and if the person interested is willing to pay such minimum bid value; the Macon-Bibb County attorney is authorized to take such action as is needful, including but not limited to, foreclosure or barring the right to redemption, to sell and dispose of the property in accordance with state law upon the stipulation that the minimum bid value as determined by the tax assessors shall be the minimum acceptable bid and that the property will in any event be sold to the highest bidder.
(c) The mayor is hereby authorized and empowered to execute quitclaim deeds to successful purchasers at such sales and the clerk is authorized to attest the mayor's signature.
2458:
(a) Whenever personal property is acquired by Macon-Bibb County at a sale for taxes, in view of the fact that under state law, title vests absolutely in Macon-Bibb County at the time of sale, the mayor shall, upon report from the tax commissioner that the property has been acquired, determine whether the property or any part thereof is useful to any department or agency of Macon-Bibb County and, if it is found to be useful, the property may be transferred to such department or agency.
(b) If the property or part thereof is not useful to Macon-Bibb County or an agency thereof, the mayor is authorized to declare the same surplus and dispose of it in accordance with state law.
2462: In recognition of the general rule that taxes voluntarily paid are not to be recovered by the payor, applications for refunds of taxes paid to Macon-Bibb County are not favored. Since the law of the state authorizes the making of refunds of taxes under certain circumstances, and in view of the obvious equity in favor of a taxpayer which may exist in certain cases, applications for tax refunds may be granted upon terms and conditions set out in this division.
2463: Applications for refund of taxes will not be favorably considered if the taxpayer has made a voluntary payment of taxes and no public officer or employee of Macon-Bibb County has done any negligent act which would mislead the taxpayer in making payment of taxes which he subsequently claims he did not owe.
2464: Ordinarily, no claim for tax refunds will be approved unless the tax sought to be refunded is duplicative of other taxes paid with respect to the same property by some other person.
2465: Even if the negligent act of a public employee contributed to the payment of taxes alleged not to be due, but the governing authority of Macon-Bibb County finds that, under all the circumstances, the negligence of the claimant was equal to or greater than the negligence act of the public officer or employee, the application for refund will be denied.
2466: If a tax refund is granted, the amount to be refunded shall not exceed the actual amount paid by the taxpayer, without interest thereon.
2467: If an applicant for a tax refund is the transferee of tax fi. fa. or has acquired the property by tax deed, it shall be a condition precedent to the payment of any refund which may be approved that the taxpayer retransfer the tax fi. fa. to Macon-Bibb County or quitclaim the property to Macon-Bibb County, as may be appropriate.
2468: No claim for tax refund shall be approved where the taxes alleged to have been erroneously paid or collected were paid more than three years prior to the date of filing of the application for refund with the governing authority, nor shall any refund be granted with respect to any taxes for any tax year, regardless of the date of payment, which is more than seven years prior to the date of filing the application for refund.
2469: The enumeration of factors to be considered in determining whether or not the Macon-Bibb County will approve a refund of taxes is illustrative and not exclusive, the restructured government reserving the right to make in the exercise of sound discretion, a determination to approve or deny such applications on sound equitable principles whether or not expressly set forth elsewhere in this division.
2472: This article is enacted pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 48-4-75 et seq. in addition to and as an alternative to non-judicial tax foreclosure. The tax commissioner is authorized to undertake judicial in rem foreclosure of delinquent ad valorem tax executions.
2473: Should any portion of this division conflict with state law, the applicable state law will control. State law only controls the conflicting portion of the division; the non-conflicting portions remain unaffected.

2477:
(a) At any time prior to sale, any interested party may redeem the property by payment of the redemption amount to the petitioner, whereupon the petitioner shall dismiss the proceedings.
(b) Following the hearing and order of the court in accordance with O.C.G.A. § 48-4-79, a sale of the property shall be advertised and conducted on the date, time, place and manner which are required by law of sheriff's sales. Such sale shall not occur earlier than 45 days following the date of the order.
(c) Except as otherwise authorized by law, the minimum bid price shall be the redemption amount. In the absence of a higher bid, the petitioner may continue the sale to a specific advertised time on the same sale date or may resubmit advertisement to sell the following month. The commission may designate a department head to bid in an amount equal to the minimum bid price and thereby become the purchaser on behalf of Macon-Bibb County.
(d) From and after the moment of the sale and tender of the successful bid price, the sale shall be final and binding, subject only to the right of the owner of the property to redeem the property upon payment into the court of the full amount of the minimum bid price. Such right of redemption of the owner shall exist for a period of 60 days from and after the date of the sale and shall be in accordance with the following provisions:
(1) Redemption by an owner shall result in a dismissal of the proceedings, and the petitioner shall refund to the purchaser the full amount paid by the purchaser at the sale;
(2) For purpose of redemption, "owner" shall mean the owner of record of fee simple interest in the property as of the date of filing of the petition, together with such owner's successors in interest by death or operation of law. This right of redemption shall not otherwise be transferable; and
(3) This right of redemption shall automatically terminate and expire upon failure to redeem within the 60-day period after the sale.
(e) If the property is not redeemed, then within 90 days after the sale, the tax commissioner shall cause to be executed and delivered to the purchaser a tax deed, together with a real estate transfer tax form.
(f) Within 90 days after the sale, the petitioner shall file a report of the sale with the court, stating whether a sale took place, the sale price, and the identity of the purchaser.
(g) If the sale price exceeds the minimum bid amount, the petitioner shall deposit the surplus into the registry of the court. Such surplus shall be distributed by the court to the interested parties, including the owner, as their interests appear and in the priority in which their interests exist.
2478:

2481:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Due date means from the 20th day after the close of the monthly period for which tax is to be computed.
Guest room means a room occupied, or intended, arranged or designed for occupancy, by one or more occupants for the purpose of living quarters or residential use.
Hotel means any structure or any portion of a structure, including any lodginghouse, roominghouse, dormitory, Turkish bath, bachelor hotel, studio hotel, motel, motor hotel, auto court, inn, public club or private club containing guest rooms and which is occupied, or is intended or designed for occupancy, by guests, whether rent is paid in money, goods, labor or otherwise. It does not include any jail, hospital, asylum, sanitarium, orphanage, prison, detention or other building in which human beings are housed and detained under legal restraint.
Monthly period means the calendar months of any year.
Occupancy means the use or possession, or the right to the use or possession of the furnishings or to the services and accommodations accompanying the use and possession of the room.
Occupant means any person who, for a consideration, uses, possesses, or has the right to use or possess any room in a hotel under any lease, concession, permit, right of access, license to use or other agreement, or otherwise.
Operator means any person operating a hotel in Macon-Bibb County including, but not limited to, the owner or proprietor of such premises, lessee, sublessee, lender in possession, licensee or any other person otherwise operating such hotel.
Permanent resident means any occupant as of a given date who has or shall have occupied or has or shall have the right of occupancy of any guest room in a hotel for at least the thirty consecutive days immediately preceding such date.
Person means an individual, firm, partnership, joint association, social club, fraternal organization, joint stock company, corporation, nonprofit corporation or cooperative nonprofit membership, estate, trust, business trust, receiver, trustee, syndicate, or any other group or combination acting as a unit, the plural as well as the singular number, excepting the United States of America, the state, and any political subdivision of either, upon which Macon-Bibb County is without power to impose the tax provided in this article.
Rent means the consideration received for occupancy valued in money, whether received in money or otherwise, including all receipts, cash, credits, and property or services of any kind or nature, and also the amount for which credit is allowed by the operator to the occupant, without any deduction therefrom whatsoever.
Return means any return filed or required to be filed as provided in this article.
Tax means the tax imposed by this article.

2483:
(a) The commission hereby finds, determines and declares that:
(1) The encouragement, development, growth and expansion of tourism and conventions within Macon-Bibb County are important to the economy of Macon-Bibb County and to the general welfare of its citizens;
(2) Macon-Bibb County should be a tourism and convention center of the state and should have the financial ability to attract and promote tourism and conventions, and to provide the necessary public facilities to compete in the domestic and international travel and convention markets; and
(3) The tourism and convention industry should pay for the delivery of the services and facilities requested by them to promote and attract visitors and convention delegates.
(b) Visit Macon, Inc., and the Macon Georgia Cherry Blossom Festival, Inc., are entities which encourage, develop and expand tourism and conventions within Macon-Bibb County to the benefit of the economy of Macon-Bibb County and the general welfare of its citizens and promote Macon-Bibb County as a tourism and convention center of the state and are essential to allow Macon-Bibb County to compete in the domestic and international travel and convention industry and also to promote and attract visitors and convention delegates to Macon-Bibb County. Such activities constitute promoting tourism, conventions and trade shows within the meaning of O.C.G.A. § 48-13-50.2(4). The Cherry Blossom Festival, Tobesofkee Recreation Area, the Macon Centreplex, the Georgia Sports Hall of Fame, the Douglass Theatre, the Tubman Museum, and the Museum of Arts and Sciences are all facilities and physical attractions which are available and open to the public and which improve destination appeal to visitors, support visitors' experience, and are used by visitors, the support of which constitutes tourism product development pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 48-13-50.2(6), as well as, to the extent applicable, promoting tourism, conventions and trade shows within the meaning of O.C.G.A. § 48-13-50.2(4).
(c) Visit Macon, Inc., is hereby designated the official destination marketing organization of Macon-Bibb County, pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 48-13-50.2(1) and O.C.G.A. § 48-13-51(b)(5)(A).
(Ord. No. O-19-0035, § 1, 6-18-2019)

2485: Every operator maintaining a hotel in Macon-Bibb County and renting guest rooms in Macon-Bibb County, not exempted under section 26-86, shall collect the tax from the occupant.
2486: No tax shall be imposed under this article with respect to occupancy by a permanent resident.
2487: Every person engaging or about to engage in business as an operator of a hotel in Macon-Bibb County shall immediately register with the tax commissioner, on a form provided by the tax commissioner. Such registration shall set forth the name under which such person transacts business or intends to transact business, the location of the place or places of business and such other information which would facilitate the collection of the tax as the tax commissioner may require. The registration shall be signed by the owner, if a natural person; in case of ownership by an association or partnership, by a member or a partner; in the case of ownership by a corporation, by an officer thereof. The tax commissioner shall, after such registration, issue without charge a certificate of authority to each operator to collect the tax from the occupant. A separate registration shall be required for each place of business of an operator. Each certificate shall state the name and location of the business to which it is applicable.
2488:
(a) Due date of taxes. All amounts of such taxes shall be due and payable to the tax commissioner monthly on or before the 20th day of every month next succeeding each respective monthly period as set forth in section 26-81.
(b) Return; time of filing; persons required to file; contents. On or before the 20th day of the month following each monthly period, a return for the preceding monthly period shall be filed with the tax commissioner showing the gross rent, rent from permanent residents, taxable rent, amount of tax collected or otherwise due for the related period, and such other information as may be required by the tax commissioner.
(c) Collection fee allowed operators. Operators collecting the tax shall be allowed a percentage of the tax due and accounted for and shall be reimbursed in the form of a deduction in submitting, reporting and payment of the amount due, if that amount is not delinquent at the time of payment, pursuant to, and at the rate authorized under, O.C.G.A. § 48-13-52.
2489:
(a) Recomputation of tax; authority to make; basis of recomputation. If the tax commissioner is not satisfied with the return or returns of the tax or the amount of the tax required to be paid to Macon-Bibb County by any person, the tax commissioner may compute and determine the amount required to be paid upon the basis of any information within his possession or that may come into his possession. One or more deficiency determinations may be made of the account due for one or more monthly periods.
(b) Interest of deficiency. The amount of the determination shall bear interest at the rate of one percent per month, or fraction thereof from the due date of taxes.
(c) Notice of determination; service of. The tax commissioner shall give to the operator written notice of his determination. The notice may be served personally or by mail; if by mail, such service shall be addressed to the operator at his address as it appears in the records of the tax commissioner. Service by mail is complete when delivered by certified mail with a receipt signed by addressee.
(d) Time within which notice of deficiency determination to be mailed. Except in the case of failure to make a return, every notice of a deficiency determination shall be mailed within three years after the 20th day of the calendar month following the monthly period for which the amount is proposed to be determined, or within three years after the return is filed, whichever period should last expire.
2490:
(a) Estimate of gross receipts. If any person fails to make a return, the tax commissioner shall make an estimate of the amount of the gross receipts of the person, or as the case may be, of the amount of the total rentals in Macon-Bibb County which are subject to the tax. The estimate shall be made for the period or periods in respect to which the person failed to make the return and shall be based upon any information which is or may come into the possession of the tax commissioner. Written notice shall be given in the manner prescribed in section 26-89(c).
(b) Interest on amount found due. The amount of the determination shall bear interest at the rate of one percent per month, or fraction thereof, from the 20th day of the month following the monthly period, for which the amount or any portion thereof should have been returned, until the date of payment.
2491:
(a) When any operator fails to make any return or to pay the full amount of the tax of five percent or $5.00, whichever is greater, if the failure is for not more than 30 days, add an additional five percent or $5.00, whichever is greater, for each additional 30 days or fraction of 30 days during which the failure continues. The penalty for any single violation shall not exceed 25 percent or $25.00 in the aggregate, whichever is greater.
(b) If the failure is due to providential cause shown to the satisfaction of the tax commissioner in affidavit form attached to the return and remittance is made within ten days of the due date, the return may be accepted exclusive of penalties.
(c) In the case of a false or fraudulent return or of a failure to file a return where willful intent exists to defraud Macon-Bibb County of any tax due under this article, a penalty of 50 percent of the tax due shall be assessed.
(d) The penalty authorized by this section shall be in addition in and not in lieu of any other penalties provided by law, including, but not limited to, the criminal penalties authorized by O.C.G.A. §§ 48-13-58 through 48-13-63, inclusive.
2492:
(a) Final return. If any operator liable for any tax, interest, or penalty imposed by this article sells or quits the business, he or she shall make a final return and payment within 15 days after the date of selling or quitting the business.
(b) Successor to withhold amount due. The operator's successor or assigns, if any, shall withhold a sufficient amount of the purchase money to cover the amount of the taxes, interest, and penalties due under this article and unpaid until the former owner produces either a receipt from the tax commissioner showing that the taxes, interest, and penalties due under this article have been paid or a certificate from the tax commissioner stating that no tax, interest, or penalty is due under this article.
(c) Liability of successor. If the purchaser of the business fails to withhold the purchase money as required by this section, he or she shall be personally liable for the payment of any taxes, interest, and penalties accruing under this article and unpaid by any former owner or assignor. The personal liability of the purchaser in such case shall not exceed the amount of the total purchase money, but the property being transferred shall in all cases be subject to the full amount of the tax lien arising from the delinquencies of the former owner. Paid executions may be transferred and enforced as otherwise provided by law.
2493:
(a) Action for tax; time for. At any time within three years after any tax or any amount of tax required to be collected becomes due and payable and at any time within three years after the delinquency of any tax or any amount of tax required to be collected, the tax commissioner may bring an action in, in the name of Macon-Bibb County to collect the amount delinquent together with interest, penalties, court fees, filing fees, attorneys' fees and other legal fees incident thereto. Such amounts and fees shall constitute a lien against the property in the same manner as ad valorem taxes as set forth in section 26-31.
(b) Duty of successors or assignees of operator to withhold tax from purchase money. If any operator liable for any amount under this article sells out his business or quits the business, his successors or assigns shall withhold sufficient of the purchase price to cover such amount until the former owner produces a receipt from the tax commissioner showing that he or she has been paid or a certificate stating that no amount is due.
(c) Liability for failure to withhold; certificate of notice of amount due; time to enforce successor's liability. If the purchase of a business fails to withhold purchase price as required, he or she shall be personally liable for the payment of the amount required to be withheld by him or her to the extent of the purchase price.
(d) Tax credit, or interest paid more than once, or erroneously or illegally collected. Whenever the amount of any tax or interest has been paid more than once, or has been erroneously or illegally collected or received by Macon-Bibb County under this chapter, it may be offset by the tax commissioner. If the operator or person determines that he or she has overpaid or paid more than once, which fact has not been determined by the tax commissioner, he or she will have three years from the date of payment to file claim in writing stating the specific ground upon which claim is founded. The claim shall be audited. If the claim is approved by the tax commissioner, the excess amount paid Macon-Bibb County may be credited on any amounts then due and payable from the person by whom it was paid, or his administrators or executors.
(Ord. No. O-22-0006, § 2, 2-15-2022)

2501:

2503:

2504:

2507: It is the purpose of this article to exercise the powers granted to the commission to levy a business license tax upon all depository financial institutions located within Macon-Bibb County in accordance with the provisions of O.C.G.A. § 48-6-93. The terms used in this article shall have the same meanings as similar language contained in such statute.
2508: For each year there is hereby levied an annual business license tax upon all depository financial institutions located within Macon-Bibb County.
2509: The tax hereby levied shall be at the rate of one-quarter of a percent of gross receipts.
2510: Notwithstanding the foregoing, the minimum amount hereby levied upon each depository financial institution for any year shall be $1,000.00.
2511: Each depository financial institution shall file an annual return of its gross receipts with the tax commissioner on or before March 1 of the year following the year in which such gross receipts are measured. Such return shall be in the manner and in the form prescribed by the commissioner of the department of revenue and shall be based upon the allocation method prescribed by law. The tax hereby levied shall be assessed and collected based upon the information provided in the return; provided, however, that if otherwise authorized by law, nothing contained in this article shall prohibit Macon-Bibb County or the tax commissioner from taking reasonable steps to confirm the information set out in the returns, and to make such adjustments in the tax reported to be due as the circumstances warrant.
2512: The tax levied hereby shall be due and payable on or before 30 days after the filing of the return to the tax commissioner. Taxes which are not timely paid shall be in default, and shall bear interest and be subject to such costs as are from time to time provided by this Code for delinquent ad valorem taxes. Taxes delinquent under the provisions of this article shall be subject to fi. fa. and collected in the same manner as ad valorem taxes in Macon-Bibb County.
2515:
For the year 1996 and succeeding years thereafter, each person who is engaged in any business, trade, profession, or occupation in Macon-Bibb County, or, to the extent required pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 48-13-7 and § 26-209 herein, in the case of an out-of-state business with no location in the state, shall pay an occupation tax for said business, trade, profession, or occupation. A business registration certificate shall be displayed in a conspicuous place in the place of business if the taxpayer has a permanent business location in Macon-Bibb County. If the taxpayer has no permanent business location in Macon-Bibb County, such business tax registration shall be shown to the Tax Commissioner of Macon-Bibb County, or their agents, upon request.
(Ord. of 10-19-2021(1), § 2)
2516:

The occupation tax applies to all businesses and occupations not specifically excluded by the provisions of O.C.G.A. §§ 48-13-5 to 48-13-26. All other applicable businesses and occupations are taxed by the local government pursuant to the pertinent general and/or local law and ordinance.
(Ord. of 10-19-2021(1), § 2)
2517:
The amount of occupation tax shall be due yearly and payable to Macon-Bibb County, at the office the Tax Commissioner, on or before March 31st of each calendar year and delinquent if not paid on or before that date.
